result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street with sidewalks and mature street trees on both sides. While the narrow geometry naturally slows traffic, the environment lacks marked crossings and is heavily obstructed by continuous on-street parking.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking on both sides of the narrow street creates significant blind spots, making it difficult for drivers to see pedestrians, especially children, stepping into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible street.

hazards.name: Lack of Designated Crossings
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross mid-block without clear right-of-way.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections and potential crossing points to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian crossing areas.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential intersection with sidewalks and a marked crosswalk. While the narrow street geometry likely encourages low vehicle speeds, significant visual obstructions are created by a large tree and a parked vehicle near the crossing point.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction (Vegetation)
hazards.description: A large tree with a low-hanging canopy significantly blocks the sightline between pedestrians at the corner and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, overhanging the sidewalk and street corner

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction (Parked Vehicle)
hazards.description: The white car parked close to the intersection limits visibility for both pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Prune the lower branches of the street tree to clear the visual zone for pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extension
interventions.description: Install a bulb-out to physically prevent parking near the crosswalk and shorten the crossing distance.

result.summary: The image shows an urban street with sidewalks on both sides and mature trees, but lacks marked pedestrian crossings or traffic control devices. Parked cars along the curb create potential sightline obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross the roadway.

result.summary: The image depicts a narrow urban intersection with sidewalks that are significantly obstructed by utility poles and parked vehicles. There is a complete absence of pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or traffic control signals.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The absence of curb ramps at the intersection creates a significant barrier for people with mobility impairments.

hazards.description: Parked cars near the intersection corner block sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
